title: Linear Programming
summary: A linear programming problem (LPP) maximises or minimises a linear objective function Z = ax + by subject to linear constraints (inequalities) and x, y ≥ 0. The variables x, y are the decision variables.

Name the quantities to be decided, write the objective (profit to maximise or cost to minimise), and turn each resource limit or requirement into an inequality. Percentages become decimals: 10% nitrogen in x kg gives 0.1x.

Draw each constraint as a line, shade the side that satisfies it, and find the feasible region common to all. The optimum of Z always occurs at a corner point of the feasible region (if it exists). Evaluate Z at every corner and pick the largest (max) or smallest (min) value. If two adjacent corners give the same optimum, every point on the segment joining them is optimal.
For an unbounded region, a minimum found at a corner is valid only if the half-plane Z < that value has no point in common with the region.
mcq: The optimum value of the objective function of an LPP occurs —
at a corner point of the feasible region
The feasible region has corners (0, 0), (6, 0), (4, 4) and (0, 5). The maximum of Z = 3x + 8y occurs at —
every point of the segment from (4, 4) to (6, 0)
Which of the following is NOT part of an LPP?
objective: (a) The common region satisfying all constraints is the ______ region. (b) Z = 2x + 3y at corner points (0, 0), (4, 0), (0, 3) and (3, 2) is maximum at ______.
vsa: A firm makes chairs (x) and tables (y). Each chair needs 2 hours and each table 3 hours; 30 hours are available. Profit is ₹40 per chair and ₹70 per table. Formulate the LPP.

Maximise Z = 40x + 70y
subject to 2x + 3y ≤ 30, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.
sa: A dealer has ₹5760 to buy fans (₹360 each) and sewing machines (₹240 each), and space for at most 20 items. Profit is ₹22 per fan and ₹18 per machine. Formulate the LPP and find the maximum profit.

Maximise Z = 22x + 18y subject to 360x + 240y ≤ 5760 (3x + 2y ≤ 48), x + y ≤ 20, x, y ≥ 0.
Corners: (0, 0), (16, 0), (8, 12), (0, 20).
Z: 0, 352, 176 + 216 = 392, 360.
Maximum profit ₹392 with 8 fans and 12 sewing machines.
la: Find the maximum and minimum of Z = x + 2y subject to x + 2y ≥ 100, 2x − y ≤ 0, 2x + y ≤ 200, x, y ≥ 0, graphically.

Corners of the feasible region: x + 2y = 100 meets x = 0 at (0, 50) and 2x − y = 0 at (20, 40); 2x − y = 0 meets 2x + y = 200 at (50, 100); 2x + y = 200 meets x = 0 at (0, 200).
Z(0, 50) = 100, Z(20, 40) = 100, Z(50, 100) = 250, Z(0, 200) = 400.
Maximum 400 at (0, 200); minimum 100 at every point of the segment joining (0, 50) and (20, 40).

or: A drink needs at least 80 units of chemical A and 60 units of chemical B. Supplier S's packet has 4 units of A and 2 of B and costs ₹10; supplier T's has 1 of A and 1 of B and costs ₹4. Formulate the LPP and find the minimum cost.

Let x packets from S and y from T. Minimise C = 10x + 4y
subject to 4x + y ≥ 80, 2x + y ≥ 60, x, y ≥ 0.
Corners of the (unbounded) region: (0, 80), (10, 40), (30, 0).
C = 320, 260, 300 ⇒ minimum ₹260 at x = 10, y = 40.

la: Minimise and maximise Z = 5x + 2y subject to x − 2y ≤ 2, 3x + 2y ≤ 12, −3x + 2y ≤ 3, x, y ≥ 0.

A machine makes products A and B. A needs 2 units of chemical and 1 of compound; B needs 1 of chemical and 2 of compound. 800 units of chemical and 1000 of compound are available. Profit is ₹30 on A and ₹20 on B. Find the maximum profit.

or: Nuts take 1 h on machine A and 3 h on B; bolts take 3 h on A and 1 h on B. Each machine runs at most 12 h a day. Profit ₹17.50 per package of nuts and ₹7 per package of bolts. Maximise profit.

Maximise Z = 17.5x + 7y subject to x + 3y ≤ 12, 3x + y ≤ 12, x, y ≥ 0.
Corners: (0, 0), (4, 0), (3, 3), (0, 4).
Z: 0, 70, 52.5 + 21 = 73.5, 28.
Maximum ₹73.50 with 3 packages of each.

la: Maximise Z = 3x + 4y subject to 2x + y ≤ 1000, x + y ≤ 800, x ≤ 400, y ≤ 700, x, y ≥ 0.

or: Fertiliser A has 12% nitrogen and 5% phosphoric acid; B has 4% and 5%. At least 12 kg of each is needed. A costs ₹110/kg and B ₹48/kg. Find the minimum cost.

la: A cooperative has 50 hectares for crops A and B, with profits ₹10,500 and ₹9,000 per hectare. Herbicide use is 20 L/ha for A and 10 L/ha for B, at most 800 L. Maximise profit.

or: Minimise Z = 20x + 10y subject to x + 2y ≤ 40, 3x + y ≥ 30, 4x + 3y ≥ 60, x, y ≥ 0.
